clue.text: Smart agent about to have a sleep

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the word for an agent surrounds the nap

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A dapper secret agent is just about to take forty winks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SPY round NAP; 'to have a' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy means stylish and well turned out, as a smart dresser is.

clue.text: Cast off and start sailing the Irish lake

indicators.note: the start of the word sailing is its first letter

parts.note: a lough is the Irish word for a lake, like the Scottish loch

explanation.surface: Someone casts off the moorings and begins sailing across a lake in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast off' looks like a sailing term but is the definition: a snake casts off its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To slough is to shed, as a snake sheds its old skin.

clue.text: Oddly, all but the smallest possible have no central mass in this metal

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, of the words all but
have no central means the middle M of the word is dropped

parts.note: the minimum is the smallest amount possible
m is the scientific symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A puzzling chemistry riddle about odd minimal quantities lacking any middle mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' takes letters 1, 3 and 5 of ALL BUT, giving ALU; 'have no central' drops the middle-ish M from MINIMUM, leaving MINIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Aluminium is a light silvery element, a metal used for cans and foil.

clue.text: The ultimate in short film material

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film
the ultimate thing is the last one

explanation.surface: The very best in brief cinema stock is up for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short film' is not a brief movie: it is PIC, the shortened form of picture; 'in' puts LAST inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic is a synthetic substance, a material moulded into countless goods.

clue.text: Remarks that nothing black is of use

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
something that serves is of use

explanation.surface: Someone comments that having nothing black is actually helpful.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to comment or note aloud, so observes means makes a comment.

clue.text: One ensures there's money in designing new bar and diner

indicators.note: designing means working these letters into a new layout

explanation.surface: A restaurateur makes a profit by designing a fresh bar and dining room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designing' rearranges NEW BAR DINER; 'and' joins the fodder and 'in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The breadwinner is the earner who brings home the household's income.

clue.text: Raise expectations initially — then the French tax energy!

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word expectations

parts.note: le is the French masculine form of the
VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to lift hopes, then a jab at a French energy levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise expectations' reads as one phrase but only 'Raise' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to lift something higher.

clue.text: Little girl accepts it is crucial

indicators.note: accepts means the girl's name takes the word it inside

parts.note: Val is a short form of the girl's name Valerie

explanation.surface: A small girl agrees that something is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little girl' is a shortened name, VAL, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital means essential, of the utmost importance.

clue.text: Speak explosively, seeing son left in golf club

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

indicators.note: in means the letter for left goes inside the club

parts.note: a putter is the golf club used on the green

explanation.surface: A father sputters with rage on seeing his son abandoned at the golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: To splutter is to talk in a rapid, spitting, incoherent way, as when angry.

clue.text: Originally, open champions used length and rule of sight

indicators.note: originally means take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Open champions are said to have first relied on length and a rule of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' takes the first letters of OPEN CHAMPIONS USED LENGTH AND RULE; 'rule' belongs to the wordplay, so only 'of sight' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocular means relating to the eyes and vision.

clue.text: Cycle set in cycle stand

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters go inside the second word for cycle

parts.note: to pedal is to cycle, riding a bicycle

indicators.note: cycle tells us to churn the letters of set round into a new order

explanation.surface: A bicycle kit parked in a bike rack.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'cycle's do different jobs: the first makes EST from SET; the second is PEDAL, and 'in' puts EST inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is a base or support on which a statue or column stands.

clue.text: Shone at golf — then made a mess!

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
littered means scattered rubbish about, making a mess

explanation.surface: A golfer played brilliantly, then left rubbish all over the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittered means sparkled or gleamed brightly.

clue.text: Teachers supporting call for top organisers

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the teachers come after the call

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone or call them
masters are schoolteachers

explanation.surface: School staff back a demand for leading administrators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' is the Big Top, a circus tent, so 'top organisers' are those who run the circus ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringmasters direct the acts in a circus under its big tent.

clue.text: A rumoured fortune to share out

indicators.note: rumoured means what is heard said, the sound of the words rather than their spelling

parts.note: a fortune is a large amount of money, a lot, with the clue's opening A completing that two-word phrase

explanation.surface: Gossip about a rich legacy that must be divided among heirs.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's opening 'A' belongs with 'fortune': the phrase 'a lot', said aloud, is indistinguishable from the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or apportion shares.

clue.text: Snide reaction, displaying little regard for feelings

annotationWithheld.why: Snide reaction, displaying little regard for feelings (13): SNIDE REACTION is the full anagram fodder, so no separate word signals the anagram; 'reaction' would be both fodder and indicator, and 'displaying' belongs to the definition.
annotationWithheld.clue: Snide reaction, displaying little regard for feelings

clue.text: Country once finding any bias is punished

indicators.note: punished means the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A nation is found guilty of prejudice and penalised.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia was the former name of Ethiopia, an African nation.

clue.text: Strike-breaking lawyers finally revealed the case for a weapon

parts.note: a scab is a worker who breaks a strike
the Bar is the body of barristers, lawyers who plead in court

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word revealed

explanation.surface: Lawyers acting against strikers finally expose a hidden sword holder.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath that holds a sword or dagger.

clue.text: An Olympic term's training is provided free of charge

indicators.note: training means the letters are put through their paces into a new shape

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter, so only term is fodder

explanation.surface: An athlete's training for the Games is paid for by sponsors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' rearranges AN OLYMPIC TERM; the 's of 'term's' adds no letter and 'is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Complimentary means given gratis, like a free ticket.

clue.text: Back problem of upper-class doctor in gaol, perhaps

indicators.note: in means the class letter and doctor go inside the jumbled prison word
perhaps hints that the letters of gaol may be arranged another way

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, as in U and non-U usage
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A posh doctor in prison suffers from a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns GAOL (British spelling of jail) into LAGO; 'in' puts U and MB inside it after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the lower back.

clue.text: Sin described by the bible suppresses a run on diamonds

indicators.note: in a down clue suppresses means pressing down on top, so the bible stands above what follows
on in a down clue means placed above, so the run comes before diamonds

parts.note: AV is the Authorized Version, the King James Bible
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Scripture condemns a greedy run on the diamond market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described by' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice, extreme greed for wealth, is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Notice an opening coming

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a public notice
a vent is an opening for air or gas

explanation.surface: Someone spots a gap in a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent is an arrival, the coming of something.

clue.text: Heartlessly batter low return from sweeper

indicators.note: heartlessly means the inner letters of batter are removed, keeping its first and last letters
return means the word for low is read backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Someone cruelly beats a meek reply out of a sweeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the verb for a cow's call, MOO, which 'return' turns to OOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A broom is a brush for sweeping floors.

clue.text: Victory in about turn means having to pay

indicators.note: in means the victory word sits inside the turned word
about means the word for turn is read backwards

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A military about-turn leads to victory and the bill that follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about turn' reads as a military drill but splits: GO (a turn) is reversed by 'about' to OG, and WIN goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Owing means in debt, still due to be paid.

clue.text: Did better to dress up as arranged

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone outdid others by choosing to dress up as planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Surpassed means exceeded or outdid.

clue.text: Lively individual won at chess after a nervous start

indicators.note: after means the pieces just before it come later in the answer, behind A and N
the start of the word nervous is its first letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, an individual
a player who has mated the opponent's king has won at chess

explanation.surface: A chess player won with a lively attack despite opening jitters.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated means full of life and vigour.

clue.text: One promised to drop new leader from money matters

indicators.note: drop ... from means take a letter out of the word for money matters

parts.note: finance is the management of money

indicators.note: the leader of the word new is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to stop handing new leadership the purse strings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drop' and 'from' frame the deletion: the N, first letter of 'new', leaves FINANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiance is a man engaged, pledged to marry.

clue.text: Accommodation given to setter in disgrace!

definitions.meaning: a setter is a breed of dog, so its kennel is the accommodation
being in disfavour, as someone in trouble with a partner is said to be in the kennel

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler is sent to sleep in the kennel for misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the puzzle's compiler but is the gundog breed; 'in' links the two definitions, from the phrase 'in the doghouse'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kennel houses a gundog, and being in disfavour is called being in the kennel.

clue.text: Record a bid, then revoke

parts.note: NT, no trumps, is a bid in bridge

explanation.surface: A bidder records an offer at auction, then withdraws it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bid' is the bridge call NT (no trumps), not an auction offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw a statement or belief formally.
